git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(beadle-iru): address Copilot review findings on PR #251

- docs/gpg-signature-verification.md's intro still called
  VerifySignature "currently a hard-coded no-op" -- it's implemented
  now, just uncalled.
- ErrKeyExpiryFinding's own text ("key expiry finding") was leaking
  into user-facing error strings (e.g. "signing key rejected: key
  expiry finding: ..."). Introduced keyExpiryFinding, a wrapper whose
  Error() returns only the underlying finding's text while Unwrap()
  []error still exposes the sentinel for errors.Is classification.
- sign.go's Sign/DetachSignBody doc comments said "rejects keys
  without an expiration date" -- now also true for an expired one.
- signature_test.go's "key expired -- non-expiring owner key" subtest
  name was internally contradictory; renamed to "key expired -- no
  expiration date configured", matching what it actually exercises.

Also documents, in parseColonExpiry's comment, why the "at least one
valid signing subkey" leniency from the prior Bugbot fix does not
reopen a bypass: verified empirically against real gpg (cert-only
primary, one expired signing subkey, one valid) that gpg itself
selects only the valid subkey to sign with, and refuses to sign
entirely when every signing subkey is expired -- the real enforcement
lives in gpg's own signing/verification operations, independent of
this pre-check.

EOF
)"

HOME_DIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/bg-XXXX)/g
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR"

export GNUPGHOME="$HOME_DIR"

gpg --batch --no-tty --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase "" --quick-generate-key "Rot Test <rot@example.com>" default cert 1y 2>&1 | tail -2
FPR=$(gpg --batch --no-tty --list-keys --with-colons rot@example.com | awk -F: '/^fpr/{print $10; exit}')

# First, add a PROPERLY-EXPIRING valid signing subkey (older).
gpg --batch --no-tty --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase "" --quick-add-key "$FPR" ed25519 sign 1y 2>&1 | tail -2
sleep 2
# Then add a NON-EXPIRING signing subkey (newer -- created after).
gpg --batch --no-tty --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase "" --quick-add-key "$FPR" ed25519 sign 0 2>&1 | tail -2

echo "=== list-keys: one valid-expiring subkey (older) + one non-expiring subkey (newer) ==="
gpg --batch --no-tty --list-keys --with-colons rot@example.com

echo "=== sign now: which subkey does gpg pick? ==="
echo "test data" | gpg --batch --no-tty --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase "" --detach-sign --armor -u rot@example.com > /tmp/sig4.asc 2>/tmp/sign4.err
cat /tmp/sign4.err
gpg --batch --no-tty --list-packets /tmp/sig4.asc 2>&1 | grep -i "keyid\|issuer"
